catalog_quote: [Thesis 1.3, p.13] The corpus figures below pertain to data collected for the Wanam variety. For the other Yelmek varieties, the ones spoken in Bibikem, Woboyo and Dodalim, I have recordings of a word list and some elicitation notes. ... [2.2.5, p.32] The picture, as it emerges so far is that the varieties spoken in Wanam and Bibikem are distinct languages, whereas Woboyo and Dodalim share a language. This shared language then is in certain respects closer to the language spoken in Bibikem than to the one spoken in Wanam ... [LD&C SP24, p.13] The variety in question here is used by people from the village of Wanam, which is the northernmost of the four villages attributed to the Yelmek branch ... I will refer to this variety simply as Yelmek, instead of Wanam-Yelmek. [Thesis 3.6, p.62 -- Wanam variety] Yelmek does not use suprasegmental features to distinguish words on a lexical level. …

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: all quoted fragments are verbatim at the stated pages in the held Gregor 2021 thesis text and LD&C paper; the held primary is genuinely silent on stress for Bibikem/Woboyo/Dodalim (ch. 2 and App. C scanned). (2) Deciding source: a 2021 ANU PhD thesis with an instrumental prosody section, i.e. the best modern work on the family, but it describes Wanam Yelmek (Glottolog wana1273, already coded NO-WORD-STRESS in the catalog); for yelm1242 it is only a word list, so UNDETERMINED is the correct reading of what we hold and the languoid split (not a duplicate of wana1273) is handled correctly per Glottolog and Gregor 2.2.5. sources.quote: Bibliographic only: establishes that Tethool 2012 is the sole phonology coded to Southern Yelmek [jel] and has no shareable file; that Drabbe 1950 and Boelaars 1950 pertain to Ilwayab = Wanam; that the SIL Okaba survey covers Marind/Awyu/Maklew only.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. 2014. Bulaka River Consonants. Journal of Language Relationship 12: 31-50 (Glottolog ref 472750; open PDF from jolr.ru files/(148)jlr2014-12(31-50).pdf).
sources.quote: None. Historical reconstruction of Proto-Bulaka River consonants from Drabbe 1950 (Jelmek of 'Yelwayab' = Ilwayab/Wanam), Geurtjens 1933 (Jab), Nevermann 1952 and Lebold et al. 2010 (Maklew); no statement on stress/accent/tone anywhere in the text (grep stress|accent|tone|prosod: 0 hits). Stress marks appear only in cited Maklew forms (e.g. ΄mio, ΄mat from Drabbe/Lebold columns), none for the Jab/Southern Yelmek column.
sources.locator: pp. 31-33 (Introduction, Sources); comparative tables pp. 33 ff.

sources.note: The only phonological description of any Southern Yelmek variety (Bibikem); our UNDETERMINED verdict rests on the silence of Gregor 2021, which describes Wanam Yelmek (wana1273) and gives only word lists for Bibikem/Woboyo/Dodalim. If Tethool states a stress rule (or its absence) for Woyu it supersedes this record.
